questions.question: A loss of 12% is incurred when an article is sold for Rs. 242, To get a profit of 15%, the article should be sold for (in Rs.) =
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling Price 1 (100% − 12% = 88%) = 242

Unitary Value: 1% = 242 ÷ 88 = 2.75

Required Selling Price (100% + 15% = 115%) = 2.75 × 115

New Selling Price = 316.25

**∴ The correct answer is 316.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Selling Price (SP₁) = Rs. 242

Initial Loss = 12%

Target Profit = 15%

**Formula used:**

Cost Price (CP) = SP × [100 / (100 − Loss%)]

New Selling Price (SP₂) = CP × [(100 + Profit%) / 100]

 
• 
 
 CP
 
 SP1 (242)
 
 SP2 (?)
 

 −12% Loss
 

 +15% Profit

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = 242 × [100 / (100 − 12)]

⇒ CP = 242 × (100 / 88)

⇒ CP = 242 ÷ 0.88 = 275

⇒ SP₂ = 275 × [(100 + 15) / 100]

⇒ SP₂ = 275 × (115 / 100)

⇒ SP₂ = 275 × 1.15

⇒ SP₂ = 316.25

**∴ The correct answer is 316.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

Selling Price = Marked Price × (1 − Discount/100). The relation between CP and MP is CP/MP = (100 − D%)/(100 + P%).

Successive Discounts

Total discount for two successive discounts x% and y% = (x + y − xy/100)%.

Dishonest Dealer

Profit % = [Error / (True Value − Error)] × 100, where Error is the weight difference.</p

questions.question: If a, b and c are the median, mode and range, respectively of the data : 8, 5, 4, 3, 2, 7, 3, 10, 9, 17, 12, 3, 8, 4, then what is the value of (3a - 2b + c)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The given number = 8, 5, 4, 3, 2, 7, 3, 10, 9, 17, 12, 3, 8, 4

**Formula used:**

If n is even

Median = [(n/2)th term + (n/2 + 1) th term]/2

Mode = The number which comes most of the time

Range = The difference between the largest number and smallest number

**Calculation:**

Arrange the given number in ascending order

⇒ 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 7 8, 8, 9, 10, 12, 17

Here n = 14

Which is even

So, Median = [(7/2)th term + (7/2 + 1)]th term/2

⇒ (5 + 7)/2

⇒ (12/2)

⇒ a = 6

Now,

Mode = The number which comes most of the time

⇒ b = 3

Now,

Range = The difference between the largest number and smallest number

⇒ (17 – 2) 

⇒ c = 15

Now,

The value of (3a - 2b + c)

⇒ (3 × 6 – 2 × 3 + 15)

⇒ (18 – 6 + 15)

⇒ (33 – 6)

⇒ 27

**∴ The required value is 27**

questions.question: Amita buys 100 apples at the rate of 12 for Rs. 100.80 and 200 apples at the rate of 15 for Rs. 117. It was found that 10% of the apple spoilt. She sold all the apples at 20 for Rs. 204. Her profit percentage in the entire transaction is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Amita buys 100 apples at the rate of 12 for Rs. 100.80

Amita buys 200 apples at the rate of 15 for Rs. 117

10% of the apple spoilt.

She sold all the apples at 20 for Rs. 204

**Formula used:**

Gain = SP – CP

Gain% = Gain/CP × 100

**Calculation:**

The cost price of 12 apples = Rs. 100.80

The cost price of 1 apple = Rs. (100.80/12) = 8.4

The cost price of 100 apples = Rs. (8.4 × 100)

⇒ Rs. 840

Now,

The cost price of 15 apples = Rs. 117

The cost price of 1 apple = Rs. (117/15) = 7.8

The cost price of 200 apples = Rs. (7.8 × 200)

⇒ Rs. 1560

Total cost price of apples = Rs. (840 + 1560) = Rs. 2400

Now,

Total number of apples = (100 + 200) = 300

10% of the apple spoilt

⇒ (300 × 10/100) = 30

Remaining apples = (300 – 30) = 270

Now,

The selling price of 20 apples = Rs. 204

The selling price of 1 apple = Rs. (204/20) = 10.2

The selling price of 270 apples = Rs. (10.2 × 270)

⇒ Rs. 2754

Now,

Gain = SP – CP

⇒ Rs. (2,754 – 2,400) = Rs. 354

Gain% = Gain/CP × 100

⇒ (354/2,400 × 100)

⇒ 354/24

⇒ 14.75%

**∴ Her profit percentage in the entire transaction is 14.75%**

The ratio of the income X and Y is 2 ∶ 3, and the ratio of their expenditures 4 ∶ 5, If X and Y save Rs. 5,000 and Rs. 17,500, respectively, than what is the income (in Rs.) of X?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of the income X and Y = 2 ∶ 3

The ratio of their expenditures = 4 : 5

X and Y save Rs. 5,000 and Rs. 17,500

**Calculation:**

Let the income of X and Y be 2p and 3p respectively

Let the expenditure of X and Y be 4q and 5q respectively

According to the question

⇒ 2p – 4q = 5 000 ...(1)

And, 3p – 5q = 17 500 ....(2)

Multiplying equation (1) by 3 and equation (2) by 2, we get

⇒ 6p – 12q = 15 000 ...(3)

And, 6p – 10q = 35 000 ...(4)

Subtracting equation (3) from equation (4), we get

⇒ 2q = 20,000

⇒ q = 10,000

Putting the value of q in equation (1), we get

⇒ 2p – 4 × 10,000 = 5,000

⇒ 2p – 40,000 = 5,000

⇒ 2p = (5,000 + 40,000)

⇒ 2p = 45,000

⇒ p = 22,500

Now,

The income of X = 2p = Rs. (2 × 22,500)

⇒ Rs. 45,000

**∴ The required income of X is Rs. 45,000**

questions.question: There are three positive integers. If the average of any two of them is added to the third, the resulting sums are 181, 172 and 160. The average of the given integers is ,
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average of any two of them is added to the third, the resulting sums are 181, 172 and 160

**Formula used:**

Average = sum of observations/Number of observations

**Calculation:**

Let the three number be a, b and c

According to the question

⇒ [(a + b)/2 + c] = 181

⇒ a + b + 2c = 362 ...(1)

Now,

⇒ [(b + c)/2 + a] = 172

⇒ b + c + 2a = 344 ...(2)

Now,

⇒ [(a + c)/2 + b] = 160

⇒ a + c + 2b = 320 .....(3)

Adding equations (1), (2) and (3)

⇒ 4(a + b + c) = 1026

⇒ (a + b + c) = 256.5

Now,

The first number = (362 – 256.5) = 105.5

The second number = (344 – 256.5) = 87.5

The third number = (320 – 256.5) = 63.5

Now,

The average of the given number = (105.5 + 87.5 + 63.5)/3

⇒ (256.5/3)

⇒ 85.5

**∴ The required average of the numbers is 85.5**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** Given:-

(a + b)/2 + c = 181

∴ a + b + 2c = 362 ...(i)

b + c + 2a = 344 ...(II)

c + a + 2b = 320 ...(iii)

**Calculation:-**

Adding eqⁿ (i), (ii), (iii)

⇒ 4(a + b + c) = 1026

⇒ a + b + c = 256.5 ...(iv)

from eqⁿ (i) - eqⁿ (iv)

c = 105.5

from eqⁿ (ii) - eqⁿ (iv)

a = 87.5

fro Eqⁿ (iii) - eqⁿ (iv)

b = 63.5

∴ Average of all three = (a + b + c)/3

Average = (105.5 + 87.5 + 63.5)/3 = 85.5

∴** required average is 85.5. **

questions.question: Last year 300 students appeared for an examination from school A, and 33(1)/(3)% of the students failed. In the same year, 480 students appeared for the examination from school B,, What is the fail percentage of students from school B if a total of 60% students got passed from both schools?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total number of students in school A = 300

Number of students failed in school A = 33(1)/(3)% 

Total number of students in school B = 480

60% of the total students from schools A and B passed

**Calculation:**

Total number of students in school A = 300

Number of students failed in school A = 33(1)/(3)% 

⇒ (300 × 100/300) = 100

Now,

Total number of students in school A and B = (300 + 480) = 780

60% of the total students from schools A and B passed

⇒ (780 × 60/100)

⇒ 468

Number of failed students from school A and B = (780 – 468)

⇒ 312

Fail student from school B = (312 – 100) = 212

Fail% of students from school B = (212/480 × 100)

⇒ (265/6)

⇒ 44(1)/(6)%

**∴ The required percentage of failed students in school B is 44(1)/(6)**
